1.why: resetRecordFor requires the token’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and rejects used/expired tokens, so the code is bound to the requesting user session.

2.why: The same reset code does not work for another session/user because record.sessionId must equal the current session.id.

3.why: Password reset only clears verifiedTokenHash/auth flags on the current session and never invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS/upgrade-insecure-requests; exact latest TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords with bcrypt; contact is stored as a digest—appropriate crypto though hashing not encryption.

6.why: No real email is sent; responses use generic copy, but the training mock exposes the reset token in the page rather than a guarded email body.

7.why: Inputs are length-limited/normalized (normalizeContact, textField), JSON body size-capped, and browser output uses textContent only.

8.why: Routing is in-app hash-only; CSP form-action 'self' and no server redirects to external URLs exist.

9.why: There are no email templates rendering user HTML/scripts; user values never become HTML.

10.why: API errors are generic, but reset/MFA tokens are written into the on-page Logs panel and mock-token element.

11.why: MFA_CODE and the initial password string are hardcoded in source; only the password is then bcrypt-hashed at runtime.

12.why: Built-in default credentials work: Initial-Clinical!2025 and MFA code 472913.

13.why: Login, MFA, reset-request, and verify paths enforce attempt windows, maxima, and temporary lockouts.

14.why: Reset request always returns the same generic eligibility message whether or not the contact matches.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), are hashed at rest, and bound to sessionId/contactDigest.
